data.q: What is the primary derive macro for enabling both serialization and deserialization in serde?
data.e: Both Serialize and Deserialize are typically derived together to allow a struct to be converted to and from formats like JSON.

data.q: Which attribute renames a specific field during serialization and deserialization?
data.e: The rename attribute changes the field's name in the serialized output (e.g., JSON key) while keeping the Rust field name unchanged.

data.q: How can you skip a field during serialization but still deserialize it?
data.e: skip_serializing excludes the field only when serializing; deserialization will still populate it.

data.q: Which attribute specifies a custom function to use for serializing a field?
data.e: serialize_with points to a function that takes the field value and a serializer, allowing custom serialization logic.

data.q: In Actix-web, which extractor is used to parse a JSON request body into a serde-deserializable type?
data.e: actix_web::web::Json<T> is the standard extractor that automatically deserializes the request payload using serde.

data.q: What does #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] do when applied to a struct?
o: Renames all fields to camelCase in the serialized output
Renames the struct itself to camelCase
Renames all enum variants to camelCase
data.e: rename_all applies a case conversion rule to every field of the struct (or enum variants) during serialization and deserialization.

data.q: How do you provide a default value for a field that may be missing during deserialization?
data.e: default uses the type's Default implementation to fill in missing fields during deserialization.

data.q: Which attribute merges the fields of a nested struct into the parent struct during serialization/deserialization?
data.e: flatten causes the nested struct's fields to appear as if they were defined directly on the parent.

data.q: How do you serialize a chrono::DateTime<Utc> as an RFC3339 string using serde?
data.e: chrono provides a serde::rfc3339 module that implements the with attribute for RFC3339 formatting.

data.q: Which crate provides the derive macros for Serialize and Deserialize?
data.e: The derive macros are re-exported from serde_derive; you typically enable the "derive" feature in serde's Cargo.toml.

data.q: In Axum, which of the following can be used to extract a JSON body into a type T?
data.e: Axum re-exports Json from axum::extract and also provides it at the crate root; all three forms are valid.

data.q: How can you serialize an enum with unit variants as a simple string (e.g., "VariantName") instead of an object?
data.e: untagged serializes enum variants without any tag or wrapper; for unit variants this results in a plain string.

data.q: What is the purpose of #[serde(borrow)] on a field?
o: Allows zero-copy deserialization by borrowing data from the input
Flattens the field into the parent struct
data.e: borrow enables deserializing into types that borrow from the input (e.g., &str, &[u8]) instead of owning allocated data.

data.q: Which trait bounds are required for a type to be used as a key in a HashMap serialized with serde?
data.e: serde requires map keys to implement both Serialize and Deserialize so they can be written to and read from formats like JSON.

data.q: How do you omit a field from JSON output when its value is None?
data.e: skip_serializing_if with Option::is_none conditionally skips serialization only when the Option is None.

data.q: Which attribute allows deserializing a field from multiple possible names (aliases)?
data.e: alias adds an alternative name for deserialization; the primary name (or renamed name) is still used for serialization.
